# Question

**Is your nose getting bigger?** Sforza et al. (2011, *Forensic Sci Int*) measured external nose dimensions by digital anthropometry in Italians aged 4–80; here the 519 men of published Table 1 (grouped means by age).

## Data source

Published Table 1 grouped means by age (men); the women's table was inaccessible, so the analysis covers men only.

# Exploratory analysis

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Mean nasal height and width by age (men, 4–80)"
m = df[df["sex"] == "men"]
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.5, 4))
ax.scatter(m["age_mid"], m["height_mean_mm"], label="Nasal height", color="#4c72b0")
ax.scatter(m["age_mid"], m["width_mean_mm"], label="Nasal width", color="#c76c6c")
ax.set_xlabel("Age (years)")
ax.set_ylabel("Mean dimension (mm)")
ax.legend()
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

# Methods & results

Pearson correlations of each dimension with age (full span and adults-only), validated with 100k-replicate randomization tests.

| Association with age | r | Randomization p |
|---|---|---|
| Nasal height, ages 4–80 | 0.78 | 1.5e-4 |
| Nasal width, ages 4–80 | 0.92 | < 1e-4 |
| Nasal height, adults 18–80 | plateaus | — |
| Nasal width, adults 18–80 | **0.99** | 0.008 |

# Decision

**Yes — the nose keeps growing throughout adulthood**, and it is mainly the *width* (cartilage growth + gravity), while height plateaus after adolescence.
